session_covered: US and European sessions of Friday 13 November
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Friday 13 November. This brief is later than usual (published after the 08:15 target), and several figures were reconciled across sources; see the footnotes.
footnotes: US 10-year: Trading Economics shows 5.145% (+1.1 bp) and ANZ +1 bp to 5.14%; FNArena's table shows 5.15% (+5 bp), so the larger move is not confirmed.

Brent: FNArena shows US$96.00 (+3.77%) but Trading Economics shows US$95.84 (+0.02%); the levels agree, the change does not. The TE figure is used because it is consistent with the prior brief's Brent level (US$96.07).
Gold: FNArena shows US$3,874.34 (-2.76%) and ANZ -1.8% to US$3,884.5, while Trading Economics shows US$3,881.75 (+0.14%); levels agree, the daily change is unresolved, and the TE figure is used.
Iron ore: FNArena US$91.60 (-0.60%) used; Trading Economics shows US$91.48 (-0.13%).
AUD/USD is from a single source (Trading Economics, CFD-based). Commodity and FX prices are CFD-based reference prices.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are around 9,114, down 0.02% (FNArena and TradingView agree), pointing to a flat open: about 9,080 on the ASX 200, roughly -1.8 points or -0.02%. The ASX 200 closed Friday at 9,082.20, down 0.71% (-64.6 points), but still rose 0.68% over the week, its third straight weekly gain.

local_events: Offshore: China October industrial production, retail sales and unemployment; Japan Q3 GDP (preliminary); US Empire State manufacturing survey
No major Australian data release was identified for today
what_moved: Wall Street drifted lower, led down by technology, as a renewed chip-sector sell-off around Nvidia's leadership change and a hot producer-price reading combined with surging Treasury yields. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.91% and the S&P 500 0.40%, while the Dow edged up 0.10%. Even so, the major US averages finished the week higher. Nvidia ended the week down about 13%, with money rotating into Apple, AMD and Broadcom earlier in the week. Markets are pricing roughly an 85-89% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and the US dollar is at a multi-month high. S&P 500 sector percentages for Friday were not available from the sources checked.

news.headline: Nvidia leadership shake-up keeps pressure on chips
news.summary: Nvidia fell again and its market value slipped below US$4 trillion after reports CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, and HSBC downgraded the stock to hold, saying it will struggle until a new CEO is named.

news.headline: Hot US producer prices reinforce Fed hike bets
news.summary: October PPI rose 0.3% m/m (0.4% expected) but the annual rate was the highest since November 2022, and markets treat a 9 December Fed hike as close to certain.

news.headline: Fed's Goolsbee: central bank "has definitely got work to do" on inflation
news.summary: The Chicago Fed president's comments added to the hawkish tone as Treasury yields extended a sharp four-session rise.

news.headline: Gold and EUR/USD hit 2026 lows as US yields surge
news.summary: A stronger US dollar and rate-hike pricing weighed on gold and the euro; the dollar index is at its highest in around 19 months.

news.headline: Aussie dollar at 10-month low as yield gap flips
news.summary: Australian bond yields have fallen below US equivalents, leaving AUD/USD under pressure ahead of this week's Australian jobs data and RBA minutes.

news.headline: ASX 200 near record, with resistance flagged at 9,200-9,250
news.summary: The index has rallied about six weeks from a swing low near 8,600, with the focus on whether the RBA is near its peak rate.

news.headline: Middle East tension and oil
news.summary: Iran reportedly struck a helicopter base in Bahrain with drones over the weekend while its parliament speaker said talks remain open; Brent has hovered near US$96/bbl after briefly dipping below US$90 earlier in the week.

news.headline: Anthropic IPO and Nvidia earnings set the week's agenda
news.summary: Nvidia reports after the US close on Tuesday, and the Anthropic IPO is expected to price on Wednesday at US$70-78 per share and begin trading on Thursday.

coming_up: Tuesday 17 November (US): October retail sales and industrial production, and Nvidia earnings after the close (Wednesday morning AEDT). Wednesday 18 November (US): FOMC minutes. Australian jobs data and RBA minutes are also due this week; exact dates were not verified.
